name: Stihl MS 250
blurb: One of the best-selling homeowner saws in North America — and the model where published chain specs contradict each other most. Bar-first verification matters most here.
intro: The MS 250 is a 45.4 cc homeowner and firewood saw sold in large numbers across the US and Canada, most often with a 16″ or 18″ bar. It is also the clearest example on this site of why model-only lookups fail: the leading web results for this saw's chain disagree with each other on pitch, gauge and drive links, and shopping listings note a gauge difference between earlier and later production. We therefore publish what each source reports — side by side — and the check that resolves it.

sources.title: Affiliate buying roundup listing the MS 250 chain
Marketplace listing set for MS 250 chain

sources_note: Reported variants from: an affiliate buying roundup (smartfixhardware.com), a chainsaw blog's MS 250 pages (chainsawnerds.com), and a marketplace listing set (accio.com), all read 23 Oct 2026. Genuine Stihl chain is sold through dealers rather than online, so replacement buying runs through Oregon-equivalent loops matched on your three numbers.

bars.note: A marketplace listing gives 62 drive links for the 16″ setup. Pitch and gauge for this length are exactly what the sources argue about — read your bar stamp.

One affiliate roundup lists the MS 250 as .325″ pitch / .063″ gauge / 68 drive links; another lists 3/8″ pitch and .050″ gauge; a marketplace listing gives 72 drive links at 18″. They cannot all describe the same bar.
